- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high to prevent overbought bias.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early 30-day horizon — add 2–3% upward bias if recent 5-day average is below 30-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating strong up/down swings, model tends to lag — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and smooth transitions.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid momentum trap.
